name: truedev-workflow
description: A gated, file-backed product and engineering workflow for long-running Codex tasks.

interface.longDescription:
TrueDev Workflow keeps long Codex coding tasks on rails. Project Init turns a product or engineering specification into durable requirements, a PRD, architecture decisions, and dependency-ordered vertical slices. Lifecycle then delivers one slice at a time through context check, scope, plan, components, implementation, tests, verification, review, documentation, and closeout, stopping at five explicit approval gates.

Every transition goes through a bundled Python runner that validates local state, records who approved what and when, and refuses to approve a gate if the repository changed while it was open. A vague "continue" is never treated as approval.

Built for developers and teams who use Codex on real repositories and want reviewable checkpoints instead of one long autonomous run.

Limitations: works in Codex only and needs Git and Python 3.9 or newer. Workflow state stays in .truedev-workflow/ inside your repository; the plugin sends it nowhere. The checks are workflow guardrails, not a security boundary: anything with write access can delete the state, and Git-ignored files are not fingerprinted. Based on the MIT-licensed workflow by Igor Druzhinin (UnBergant).
defaultPrompt: Turn this specification into an approved delivery plan with $project-init.
Start the next ready slice with $lifecycle, and stop at every gate.
Show me $lifecycle status: the open gate and the next action.

publication.release_notes: Directory edition: a skills-only package without lifecycle hooks, where every approval gate is held by the runner's working-tree integrity check. Both editions now refuse to approve a gate whose evidence changed after it opened, hold every transition while the compact checkpoint is open, and are gated to Codex.
